name: rubric
rubric: A Brief is written before any research and is the yardstick every later artifact is judged against, so each goal is concrete enough to judge a Dossier by. Its Slides are the spine write-dossier keeps. Fail if a goal is too vague to judge a Dossier against.

body: type: brief; the body states goals before writing.

The two process:markdown-harness entries also predate this run's checks (run began 2026-10-14T16:24:58Z). The draft therefore reads as approved before the draft-brief gate opens.

name: rubric
rubric: The sections a Brief must settle, in reading order, so the grill knows what is left and research starts from settled questions. Fail if a section holds what belongs in a different one.
body: All sections hold their own material: Format/Audience/Style/Learning goal/Actionables/Hook/Red thread/Analogy/Constraints/Slides/Research questions/Episode Design Reference/Open ideas in template order, no undefined headings (mh clean).

name: rubric
rubric: The working title of the Episode, naming its subject. Fail if it names the Format or a process instead of the subject.
body: h1 'Why it's never too early to start with sales' names the subject, not the Format or a process.

name: rubric
rubric: Foundations, Teardown or Short, and the planned duration; together they set the scale of everything below. Fail if either is missing.
body: 'Foundations, 20-30 minutes.' names Format and duration.

name: rubric
rubric: Who watches, what they already know and what they want, so every later choice can be judged against them. Fail if it names a group without saying what they know or want.
body: Names early-stage founders and founding-team members, says they know they 'should sell' but treat sales as later-stage, and want concrete reasons to start now and a first method.

name: rubric
rubric: One line naming a style from docs/design/design-guide.md and the audience reason for it; the designers keep that style for the whole Episode. Fail if it names no style, names none the design guide lists, or gives no audience reason.
body: Style names 'Board', but docs/design/design-guide.md '## Named styles' lists only 'Editorial'. The audience reason is present (founders plan on whiteboards and sticky notes). The guide says 'A new style is added when an Episode uses one', so Han decides: add Board to the design guide, or pick Editorial (also his Open idea).

name: rubric
rubric: What the viewer can do or explain afterwards, in one or two sentences, the end every Section moves towards. Fail if it names a topic to cover instead of a change in the viewer.
body: 'Explain why sales must start long before revenue is needed, and name the first concrete steps to build a sales pipeline.' is a change in the viewer, two clauses in one sentence.

name: rubric
rubric: Concrete steps a viewer takes after watching, one per item; each is later backed by at least one Slide. Fail if an item is a belief or a topic instead of a step a viewer could take.
body: All four items are steps (build a cashflow view, start lead generation, make first contact, track deals). Backing: 1 by Slides 1/6/10, 2 and 3 by Slide 3, 4 by Slides 7-8.

name: rubric
rubric: The opening that earns the first thirty seconds. Fail if it only announces the topic instead of giving the viewer a reason to stay.
body: 'The cashflow board that goes bankrupt in March because the big revenue only lands in April.' gives a concrete stake, not a topic announcement.

name: rubric
rubric: The single line of argument from the hook to the learning goal, which every Section advances. Fail if it lists topics instead of making one argument, or does not end at the learning goal.
body: One argument: revenue lags costs, so by the time you feel you need sales it is too late; ends at 'start the pipeline before you need the money', the why-half of the Learning goal.

name: rubric
rubric: Two Threads told in turns so the audience never follows one too long, chosen in the grill by planned duration in any Format.
body: Threads is optional and absent; A/B Threads sit only in Open ideas. Nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: The first Thread, usually the mechanism or argument. Fail if it does not carry the Red thread.
body: No A thread heading (Threads absent); nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: The second Thread, told in turns with the A thread and strengthening it. Fail if cutting it would not weaken the A thread.
body: No B thread heading (Threads absent); nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: One everyday picture the Episode returns to, giving the abstract idea a handle; a list keeps the parts of the picture as Han said them. Fail if picturing it takes expertise, or it offers several pictures.
body: One everyday picture: the monthly cashflow sticky-note board (cash, cost, revenue), used on Slides 1, 6, 10; needs no expertise.

name: rubric
rubric: Story rules every Slide obeys, one per item, so a writing job and its reviewer check each Slide against them. Fail if an item governs a single Slide, which belongs in that Slide's purpose.
body: Three items, each a rule for every Slide (no dated claims; works live and on YouTube; start from the source deck and draw own visuals). None governs a single Slide.

name: rubric
rubric: The spine Han settled: one h3 per Section, each an ordered list of its page Slides, numbered on across Sections. Each item is `**<title>** — <purpose>. _Visual:_ <idea>`, with an optional `_Research:_ <n, m>` naming the research questions it rests on, and a leading `(A)` or `(B)` when the Brief has Threads; the staging test checks that shape. write-dossier keeps this spine. Fail if a purpose advances no step of the Red thread, the Slides take its steps out of argument order, the first Slide does not carry the Hook, or the last Section does not land the Learning goal.
body: Shape passes the staging test; Slide 1 carries the Hook; last Section (Slide 10) lands the why-half of the Learning goal. Han to judge argument order: 'Pipeline tools in practice' (4) and 'How marketing feeds the pipeline' (5) use the pipeline before 'What is a sales pipeline' (7) defines it, and the cashflow payoff 'revenue pulled in' (6) sits inside 'How to start doing sales' before the 'Why it takes time' Section.

name: rubric
rubric: A Section, titled as the table of contents names it, holding the page Slides that make one step of the Red thread. Fail if its Slides serve more than one step.
body: Sections 1, 2, 4, 5 each hold one step. Han to judge Section 'How to start doing sales': Slides 3-5 serve 'how to start' (stages, tools, marketing), while Slide 6 'Watch your cashflow, revenue pulled in' serves the cashflow consequence, a second step.

name: rubric
rubric: The questions the Episode's claims depend on, one per item, each researched on its own: a why question scoped to a subject matter. Fail if a question names the Episode, bundles two questions or asks what no claim needs, or a claim elsewhere in the Brief needs a question that is missing.
body: All seven are why questions scoped to a subject, none names the Episode, each is used by a Slide. Han to judge: Q5 'Why does engaging in sales and obtaining early sales results, like LOI, filled sales pipeline, generate trust?' may bundle two causes (engaging vs results); Slide 3's claim 'delivery adds more lag before cash arrives' cites no research question (Q1 may cover it).

name: rubric
rubric: Files (pdf, word) brought in as a model for the Episode (a deck, a sketch, miro slides export), one per item, `[<title>](reference/<file-slug>/design-reference.md)`: the file the convert-references job writes from the copy at `.scratch/<slug>/<file-slug>.<file-extension>`. Fail if an item names a file the prompt or handoff did not bring.
body: One item, the source deck, which the handoff brings (Constraints names source-deck.pdf); copied to .scratch/never-too-early-sales-run-2/source-deck.pdf; link reference/source-deck/design-reference.md matches the prescribed shape (target pending convert-references by design).

name: rubric
rubric: Ideas the grill did not settle, kept for the feedback loop; nothing here binds the run. Fail if an item restates or overrides a settled section.
body: Open idea 'The cashflow board is the spine — consider making it the recurring visual the whole Episode returns to.' restates the settled Analogy ('returned to three times across the talk') and Slides 1/6/10. Also 'Editorial style instead of Board' proposes overriding the settled Style (relevant to the Style fail).

name: rubric
rubric: The text under every heading except Episode Design Reference is Han's wording: `.scratch/<slug>/handoff.md` when it exists, his answers in this session, or a shape-only fix the run-log entry names.

name: rubric
rubric: No two sections of the Brief contradict each other, and no section contradicts itself.
body: No hard contradiction found. Han to judge: Constraint 'Start from the source deck, [source-deck.pdf](./source-deck.pdf) beside this Brief' points at a file that is not beside the Brief (copy lives at .scratch/never-too-early-sales-run-2/source-deck.pdf; the Episode Design Reference points at reference/source-deck/design-reference.md); and Format 'Live coaching slot next week' is a dated phrase next to Constraint 'Reusable across talks: no dated claims' (likely fine, since it is scheduling, not a claim).

body: 'Live coaching slot next week' (Format) changes no job's output: the scheduling date shapes no Slide, Dossier or design choice. Also Open idea 'Fix the "Sales funel" typo when the Slide is built.': Open ideas bind nothing and the Slides are drawn fresh, so no job acts on it as written.
